title: Total Cost to Hire K Workers
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array costs where costs[i] represents the cost of hiring the i-th worker, and integers k and candidates, hire exactly k workers following these rules: - You will conduct k sessions, hiring one worker in each session.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array costs where costs[i] represents the cost of hiring the i-th worker, and integers k and candidates, hire exactly k workers following these rules: - You will conduct k sessions, hiring one worker in each session. - In each session, select the worker with the lowest cost from either the first candidates workers or the last candidates workers. If there is a tie, choose the worker with the smallest index. - If fewer than candidates workers remain, hire the worker with the lowest cost among the remaining workers. In case of a tie, choose the worker with the smallest index. - Each worker can only be hired once. - The total cost of hiring the workers is to be returned.
constraints: Hire exactly k workers in k sessions.
At each session, candidates are the first and last candidates unhired workers; choose minimum cost, then smallest original index on a tie.
Return the sum of hired costs.
reference_solution:
def total_worker_hiring_cost(costs,k,candidates):
    import heapq
    left=[];right=[];i=0;j=len(costs)-1
    while i<=j and len(left)<candidates:heapq.heappush(left,(costs[i],i));i+=1
    while i<=j and len(right)<candidates:heapq.heappush(right,(costs[j],j));j-=1
    total=0
    for _ in range(k):
        if not right or left and left[0]<=right[0]:
            cost,index=heapq.heappop(left)
            if i<=j:heapq.heappush(left,(costs[i],i));i+=1
        else:
            cost,index=heapq.heappop(right)
            if i<=j:heapq.heappush(right,(costs[j],j));j-=1
        total+=cost
    return total
